sections.h2: Who bills and assesses property tax in Hoboken?
sections.html:
Hoboken's Tax Collector bills and collects every property tax in the city, and the Tax Assessor keeps the tax map plus the list of owners, mailing addresses and assessed values. A Hoboken bill rolls municipal, school, county and library taxes into one document. A property inside the Special Improvement District sees that district's assessment on the same bill. The city's taxation page and assessor page are the two to keep handy.

The assessor also runs the senior citizen, disabled person and veteran deductions. Copies of records come through the City Clerk's Office.

sections.h2: When are Hoboken property taxes due?
sections.html:
Hoboken taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, the four installment dates New Jersey sets for calendar-year municipalities in N.J.S.A. 54:4-66. The city mails a single bill each year with four payment stubs. Under the statute the first two installments are each a quarter of the prior year's tax, and the last two split whatever remains of the current levy.

The collector's page prints the grace-period end date for each quarter only as a graphic, so read the date on your stub or call ext. 1220 before you mail anything. The office does not honor postmarks. A payment must be in the office, in the drop box or paid through the city's online portal by the last day of grace. Anything later carries interest running from the original due date.

The drop box sits inside the Newark Street entrance of City Hall and is open from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on days the office is open. The office closes on city holidays and weekends.

sections.h2: What is the property tax rate in Hoboken?
sections.html:
The state's 2025 table lists Hoboken at a general rate of 1.805 and an effective rate of 1.070, the lowest effective rate of the twelve Hudson County municipalities in that table. The general rate is applied per $100 of assessed value. As a rough illustration, a home assessed at $600,000 would owe about $10,830 a year at 1.805. The effective rate restates the burden against estimated true value, which lets owners compare towns whose assessments sit at different levels.

The city introduced a $152 million municipal budget for 2026 and described a projected municipal tax impact of under 19 percent, or roughly $130 more per quarter for the average assessed property compared with 2025. Your own bill shows what was finally adopted, so use it rather than a news figure when you plan a sale.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation 2025 General Tax Rates; City of Hoboken budget announcement.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hoboken assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition of appeal with the Hudson County Board of Taxation. The appeal must be filed and received by April 1, or within 45 days of the bulk mailing of assessment notices, and the deadline moves to May 1 in a district that has just completed a revaluation or reassessment. The 2026 filing window has closed, so the next realistic target is the April 1 date in the following year.

The state's appeal guide sets the ground rules for what happens next:

  • The owner carries the burden of proof, usually with three to five comparable sales that predate the October 1 assessment date.
  • Photos of the home and of each comparable help the board see the argument.
  • The assessor and the board need copies of the comparables at least seven days before the hearing.
  • Hearings are generally held within three months of the filing deadline.
  • A reduced value is frozen for that year and the following two years unless something changes the property.

The Hoboken collector explains what a win looks like on the bill. No adjustment can be calculated until the county certifies the tax rate. The credit then goes first against fourth-quarter tax, then against any third-quarter balance, and a leftover credit is refunded to the petitioner or the attorney who filed. The first and second quarters of the next year show the lowered figure, and a revised bill goes to the owner and to the mortgage company of record.

sections.h2: Which other Hoboken tax bills fall outside the quarterly cycle?
sections.html:
A few charges do not follow the four-stub pattern, and each one can surface during a sale.

  • Added assessment and omitted tax bills. These cover improvements that raised a property's value. They are mailed in October and due November 1, with a grace period through November 10 and interest from November 1 after that.
  • Lien redemptions. Ask the collector for a redemption statement before you pay. Balances shown on the city website may be off, and payment must be by certified check or money order.
  • Returned checks. City ordinance DR-400 adds a $20 fee for a bounced check, and the office then asks for certified funds, cash or a money order.
  • Change of address. A signed request goes to the assessor at 94 Washington Street, by email, or by phone at ext. 1230.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can Hoboken homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Hudson County's tax assessment division hosts a single combined application for the Senior Freeze reimbursement, ANCHOR, the Stay NJ credit, deductions, exemptions and abatements. The Hoboken assessor takes the local deduction forms.

The state's $250 deduction for seniors and disabled persons requires age 65 or older, or disability, as of December 31 of the pretax year. The applicant must also have lived in New Jersey for a year before October 1, owned and lived in the home on October 1, and stay under the income limit. The owner files Form PD5 with the tax collector by March 1 each year to keep it. A denial can be appealed to the county board on Form A-1 by April 1 of the following year.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation senior and disabled deduction page; Hudson County Division of Tax Assessments.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Hoboken?
sections.html:
Hoboken covers 1.25 square miles of land and held 60,419 residents in the 2020 census, which works out to 48,335 people per square mile. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 59,027. Only 33.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of those homes was $895,100 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent was $2,938, and median household income was $180,579.

The city's 28,088 households average 2.02 people, and 82.6 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Mean travel time to work is 36.8 minutes. Small households, a renter majority and high values shape the market, and the street grid of named avenues crossing numbered streets holds most of the sales.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How does an unpaid tax bill affect selling a house in Hoboken?
sections.html:
A quarter left unpaid after its grace period becomes delinquent and keeps accruing interest until all taxes and liens are paid, so a seller with a past-due balance has to clear it or have the closing pay it. Request a written payoff or redemption figure from the collector close to the closing date, since interest changes the number. Ask whether any added assessment bill is still on the way if you renovated.

Taxes paid ahead of a due date are accepted at any time under the statute, and no interest builds before the delinquency date. A condominium owner should also confirm whether the Special Improvement District charge sits on the bill. A buyer who purchases as-is still receives a deed that gets recorded with the county, so settle the tax status before that step.

faqs.q: Who do I call to pay or ask about a Hoboken tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector at (201) 420-2000, ext. 1220, between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays. The office is at 94 Washington Street and is closed on city holidays and weekends.

faqs.q: Are Hoboken property taxes paid quarterly?
faqs.a: Yes. Payments fall on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, and the city sends one bill with four stubs. The office accepts no postmarks, so the payment must reach the city by the end of the grace period.

faqs.q: Is Hoboken's tax rate high compared with the rest of Hudson County?
faqs.a: No. The state's 2025 table shows Hoboken's effective rate of 1.070 as the lowest among the county's twelve municipalities. Home values are high, though, so the dollar amount of a bill can still be large.

faqs.q: What happens if my Hoboken appeal succeeds after I already paid?
faqs.a: The adjustment goes first to fourth-quarter taxes, then to any third-quarter balance, and any remaining credit is refunded. The city cannot apply it until the county certifies the tax rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hoboken house with tax still owed?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the closing pays the balance. Get a current payoff from the collector, and ask for a lien redemption statement if a lien exists, because the website balance may not be current.
